subject: Are there alternatives to PARDISO by panua

messages.author: c45fb7365242c632
messages.subject: Are there alternatives to PARDISO by panua
parts:
Hi, I have just started working on a project that uses the INLA package. 

I am working in a cluster environment and t I have managed to correctly set up the free academic PARDISO license. 

What I wanted to ask is weather there are free alternatives to the PARDISO solver by panua, for example one MKL-PARDISO by intel which I could use. 

Thank you so much

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Are there alternatives to PARDISO by panua
parts:
using PARDISO for a cluster you'll need a such license (about 1000$ a year I
think, but check please). if the default solver will run you can use that one.

PARDISO for MKL does not work, as the partial inverse require is not there (also
other features that were added for us/INLA is not there).

There is progress in developing a new sparse solver for INLA which do scale
better and is open source. this is done of one of the postdoc at the HPC group
at KAUST. the plan is that this will be the new default solver. Hopefully, its
there end of this year

H
